column2: req_desc

Blank chart by keyboard.
Tab reaches the one cursor cell of `grid "Stitch chart"` with its exact label, and the arrow keys move it one cell at a time, stopping at the chart's edges, with row 1 at the bottom.

Stitch entry follows the reading direction.
Each letter key places its symbol on the cursor and moves the cursor one cell in that row's reading direction, as qualified in Interactions.

Placed symbols are announced.
`status "Cell announcement"` reads each cursor move and each placed symbol in the published words.

Written lines change with the cells.
Each edit shows the affected written lines in the same render as its cells, and cells and lines survive a reload.

Crochet swatch by keyboard.
A crochet chart takes the crochet letter keys and its written lines swap nothing between sides.

Row rule and error list.
Every non-empty row's used stitches are checked against the nearest non-empty row below or the cast-on, and `list "Row errors"` shows each error in row order.

Row counts on the chart.
Each chart row shows the server's used, made and state values, and the same values reach every other designer's page with no reload.

Row check announcements.
`status "Row check"` reads each row error as it appears and each cleared row, in the same words the error list shows.

Publishing refused with row errors.
Publish is refused with the exact count of row errors while any remain, and colour warnings never block it.

Shaping lines.
The worked shaping chart reads as its seven printed lines, with wrong-side texts on wrong-side rows.

Counts follow each edit.
A keyboard edit changes that row's made count at once, gives the rows above their errors, and undo restores the earlier lines.

Cable cells.
The cable key places four cells that read as one item, and both cable row errors appear as published.

Crochet terms.
One crochet chart writes the printed US lines in US terms and the printed UK lines in UK terms.

Repeat detection.
Every printed repeat example reads exactly as printed from the cells given.

Repeat boxes by keyboard.
A selection and the box key make a repeat box, its times spinbutton changes counts and lines at once, and an overlapping box is refused.

Expanding a repeat.
Expanding a box widens the chart without changing any line or count, undo brings the box back, and an expansion past the column limit is refused.

Twin lift through repeats.
A token inside a repeat lifts its position in every worked repeat, following its row's working direction, exactly as in the printed example.

Text applies to the chart.
Typed text commits through the published grammar into cells, returns in canonical form, and reports the cells changed with focus back on the edit button.

Text errors name the row and position.
Text that cannot parse leaves the chart unchanged, stays as typed with the caret at the failing position, and shows the exact error.

Repeat text fills the row.
A typed repeat is worked as many whole times as the row's needed stitches allow, and one that does not fit is refused at its star.

Typing survives pushed edits.
An open text box keeps its text, caret and shown error while pushed edits land, and warns when its own row changed.

Text edits reach the co-designer.
An applied text changes the other designer's chart and written lines with no reload, and the changed cells flash.

Range selection and clipboard.
Shift and the arrow keys select a rectangle, and copy, cut and paste work on it with the published paste rule and status.

Mirror.
Mirror reverses a selection row by row, swaps the published partners and carries colours with their cells, and is refused on a selection touching a repeat box.

Undo and redo.
The undo and redo keys step through a person's actions one whole action at a time.

Paint and select by pointer.
A fast Paint drag fills every cell along its line as one undo step and one request, and a Select drag selects a rectangle with the published status.

Paint by touch.
On a 390 by 844 touch screen, taps and drags paint cells of at least 32 by 32 px, and the grid rather than the page takes the gesture.

Colour key and colour keys.
Colours are added in `list "Colour key"` up to the limit, and the digit keys colour the cursor cell or selection.

Colour in written lines.
A row of more than one colour names a colour on every item and run, and colours count when items are compared for runs and repeats.

Colour warnings.
`list "Colour warnings"` shows each colour-count and float warning in row order and clears when the row is fixed.

Presence.
`list "Here now"` and the `data-peer` mark show who is on the pattern and where, backed by the published Valkey hash.

Live edits in place.
One designer's edits, cursor moves and row checks reach the other designer's page with no reload and no scroll jump.

Conflict notice.
When two designers change one cell, the first accepted edit stands, and the refused person sees the exact notice and the server's value until the notice clears.

Undo leaves a later change alone.
Undo skips a cell another designer changed after your step and says so in the published words.

Inviting and joining.
A designer's invitation sends one mail with one link, and the tester joins from it onto the follow page, as qualified for expired and used links in Business rules.

Follow page by touch.
At 375 by 812 a tester steps rows by tap and swipe on buttons of at least 44 by 44 px, with the counter, line and buttons kept on screen.

Shared row counter.
Two devices stepping from one row move the counter once, a replayed step changes nothing, and every device of that tester shows the new row and pin with no reload.

Testers table follows live.
The designer's `table "Testers"` shows each tester's version, row and note count as they change, and each tester keeps their own row.

Tester and stranger access.
A tester reads only the version they follow and their own notes, and a stranger gets not found for any private pattern, page or API.

Row notes and notice mail.
A saved note reaches the designer's page live and sends one mail to the owner after saving, and no other tester sees it.

New-version notice.
A newly saved version shows the notice on every open follow page without changing the row, the chart or focus.

Moving to a new version.
Moving keeps the row number and shows the new line, or goes to the last row with the published status if the new version is shorter, on all of that tester's devices.

Comparing versions.
The compare page shows the exact summary line and marks every cell of the later version, by the published rule.

Restoring a version.
A restore makes a new version with cells, colours, repeats and lines identical to the original, destroys nothing later, and reaches other designers live.

Published page.
A published pattern reads at `/p/<id>` to anyone, and an unpublished one answers not found.

PDF sheet.
The app builds the PDF from the published version with the published page order, lines, key and footers.

No private data on copies.
The published page and the PDF carry no tester name, tester email address or note text.

Live notice under outage.
With Valkey unreachable the app starts, health answers 200, and every signed-in page shows the published notice in `status "Live"`.

Saved work under outage.
With Valkey unreachable, saved patterns open, and cell edits, text edits and versions save and survive a reload, while other pages get nothing until reloaded.

Counter and notes under outage.
With Valkey unreachable, counter moves save with the same from-row rule, notes save and their mail goes out, and `list "Here now"` shows only the viewer.

Accounts.
Sign-up, mail verification and sign-in work with the published fields, copy, expiry and return to the page asked for.

Published layout widths.
Designer and follow pages change `data-layout` exactly at 600 and 1024 px, with the published layout for each and no sideways page scroll.

Twin lift.
Pointer or focus on a cell or token lifts exactly that twin set at once, leaving reverses it at once, no-stitch cells never lift, and a pin stays after leaving.

Reduced motion.
Under reduced motion, from the system or from `checkbox "Reduce motion"`, every published state stays with no shift, no moving highlight and a static outline in place of flashes.

Named motion.
The follow highlight, the change flash and the version notice run for their published times with their published marks, and nothing else on the page moves.

Dialogs and focus.
Every dialog keeps Tab inside it, Escape closes it, focus returns to its opener, and focus is always visible on cells, lines and controls.

Accessibility checks.
Designer, follow and compare pages have no automated accessibility violations at 375, 768 and 1280 px wide.

Workspace look.
Every screen carries the pale shell, single bordered panel, lead line, pastel tiles and original stitch glyphs described in Visual design.

Platform and configuration.
Health, public configuration, published limits, the error order, the edit rate limit and the replayed edit behave as published in every instance.

Credentials and same origin.
Every credential is read from the environment, the browser talks only to its own origin, and fonts and icons come from the app itself.
`/app/run.json` has string `install`, `build` and `serve` commands and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` names every shipped package, font and icon set with its licence. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`).
Every shipped package, font and icon set uses an open licence: MIT, BSD, ISC, Apache-2.0 or SIL OFL.
The app uses only Postgres, Mailpit and Valkey, with no other datastore, queue or PDF service.
No page loads anything from another origin, and no web font, script or icon is fetched from a hosted service.
All server and client source is TypeScript.
No shipped package is a headless browser.
Provisioned service configuration is left as given, and no credential is committed to source.
